summary: Validated the react-native-keyboard-controller -> local shim refactor. Frontend Expo web preview builds cleanly (Metro bundled 1410 modules, no errors) and boots without red-box. All 10 imports now point at @/src/utils/keyboard; only reference to 'react-native-keyboard-controller' left in repo is expo/bundledNativeModules.json (harmless) and the doc comment inside keyboard.tsx. Guest login works; dashboard renders. All keyboard-affected input flows work end-to-end on mobile viewport (390x844): Todos FAB -> sheet -> type 'TEST_KB Task 1' -> Add task -> todo appears; Habits FAB -> sheet -> type 'TEST_KB Read daily' -> Add habit -> habit appears with heatmap; Expenses FAB -> sheet -> amount 100 -> Save entry -> -$100 shown + monthly summary updated; Reminders Water quick tile -> sheet opens with default time chips (08:00..20:30) and 'Save reminder'; EMI/SIP inputs accept values (500000/9.5/15 and 5000/12/10) inside KeyboardAwareScrollView shim; AI Chat input focuses and message sends (Gemini 3 Flash configured); AI Grammar Fixer textarea works and 'Fix grammar' button is tappable; Notes editor opens, title+body inputs work, 'Saved' auto-save indicator appears. Backend smoke passes: GET /api/ 200, POST /api/auth/guest 200 (session_token issued), POST /api/todos 200, POST /api/expenses 200.

react_native_issues.issue: Tapping 'Save reminder' on web triggers 'Notifications.getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync is not available on web' error overlay. UNRELATED to the keyboard-controller refactor — expo-notifications simply has no web implementation for scheduling. On device/Android build this works. Recommend guarding calls with Platform.OS !== 'web' (or presence check) so web preview stays crash-free. Reference: /app/frontend/app/reminders/index.tsx:35

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Guard reminders/index.tsx scheduleForReminder() with `if (Platform.OS === 'web') return;` around calls to Notifications.getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync / cancelScheduledNotificationAsync / scheduleNotificationAsync so web preview never throws. Not blocking Windows Android build (which is the actual target of this refactor).
(Optional cleanup) The 'react-native-keyboard-controller' pin still exists in node_modules/expo/bundledNativeModules.json but is dead-weight only if you re-install it accidentally; safe to ignore.
critical_code_review_comments: KeyboardStickyView shim wraps children in KeyboardAvoidingView with behavior=undefined on Android, which effectively does nothing there — this is expected fallback (native lib was doing IME-anchored positioning). For bottom-sheets the current behavior works because sheets already sit above the keyboard on Android via system inset handling; visually verified.
KeyboardAwareScrollView shim ignores `bottomOffset` prop (kept for API compatibility). Fine for current forms (EMI/SIP/Notes/AI tool) which don't need extra bottom offset.
Root layout still wraps app in KeyboardProvider from the shim — the provider is a no-op fragment, so this is a harmless placeholder; can be deleted later if you want to fully remove the reference.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of keyboard flows (Todos, Habits, Expenses, Reminders sheet, EMI, SIP, AI Chat, AI Tool, Notes editor)

seed_data_creation: Guest 'TEST_KBShim' with 1 todo, 1 expense created via API. Guest via UI created 1 habit 'TEST_KB Read daily', 1 note 'TEST_KB Note Title'. Left in DB (small volume, prefixed TEST_KB for easy identification).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Keyboard shim at /app/frontend/src/utils/keyboard.tsx exports KeyboardAvoidingView, KeyboardStickyView, KeyboardAwareScrollView, KeyboardProvider. All app imports now use @/src/utils/keyboard. The single web-only crash on Reminders 'Save' is a pre-existing expo-notifications web limitation (getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync not implemented on web) — not introduced by this refactor. Backend base URL: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env.
rca_of_issue: N/A — refactor validated as working. The one error observed (Reminders save on web) is orthogonal to the keyboard-controller removal and rooted in expo-notifications lacking a web implementation for scheduling APIs.
